title: Météo : 2025, le troisième été le plus chaud de l'histoire en Tarn-et-Garonne après 2022 et 2003
content: The meteorological assessment of the 2025 summer in Tarn‑et‑Garonne, covering 1 June to 31 August, shows that it was the third hottest on record for the region.  The average maximum temperature reached 29.7 °C, with the peak daily maximum on 11 August recorded at 42 °C – the third highest ever measured in the commune.  In Montauban the same day the thermometer read 41.8 °C, while in Caylus it reached 40.7 °C.  The 2023 summer, which also featured a heatwave, had a comparable average maximum of 29.7 °C.  The two previous record summers were 2022 (32 °C) and 2003 (31.9 °C), as noted by the MétéoFrance technician: 'Seules les années 2022 avec 32°C et 2003 avec 31,9°C sont au-dessus depuis le début de nos relevés à Montauban, en 1963. Il y a malgré tout une énorme différence avec ces deux valeurs-là'.  Minimum temperatures followed a similar pattern, with 2025’s average low of 17.1 °C ranking just below 2003 (18.5 °C), 2022 (17.4 °C) and 2023 (17.2 °C).  July experienced a severe drought, with only 12 mm of rainfall recorded in Montauban compared to a 60‑year average of 47 mm, according to Valéry Moutot: 'Pour la station de Montauban, on a ainsi relevé 12 mm de précipitations seulement, contre une moyenne de 47 mm sur les 60 dernières années'.  June 2025 received 55 mm, slightly below the 68 mm average, while August saw 68 mm, surpassing the 55 mm average.  Moutot cautioned against generalising these figures across the department: 'Il est néanmoins très dangereux, sur cette donnée, d'extrapoler avec l'ensemble du département, altère le météorologiste'.  Overall, the 2025 summer was described as 'bien ensoleillé' and its insolation ranked 12th among the last 35 years.

title: Météo. Canicule, sécheresse et records... voilà les chiffres de l'été 2025 en Occitanie
content: Nationally, the 2025 summer was the third warmest since 1900, with a temperature anomaly of +1.9 °C, behind 2003 (+2.7 °C) and 2022 (+2.3 °C). June was especially hot, +3.3 °C, just below June 2003 (+3.6 °C). Rainfall fell 15 % overall, with the southern half sometimes down 50 %. Solar radiation was 10 % above normal. The season included 27 heat‑wave days, ranking second only to 2022’s 33 days. In Occitanie, temperatures were the highest in France, averaging +2.1 °C above the 1991‑2020 normal, matching the national record set in Nouvelle‑Aquitaine. Sunshine was near normal: 579 h (+5 %) in Toulouse and 990 h (+5 %) in Nîmes. Precipitation was 15 % below the regional average; Perpignan received 99 mm, a 50 % excess. Intense rainfall events included 90 mm on 12 July in Ille‑sur‑Têt and 154 mm on 31 August in Cavillargues. Météo France noted that the 35 °C threshold was exceeded in more than 80 % of the territory, ‘Le seuil des 35°C a été atteint sur plus de 80 % du territoire…’, and that in the south it was exceeded one day in four, sometimes one day in three (e.g., Nîmes). Nîmes was 2.1 °C above normal, Carcassonne +2.4 °C, Mende +3.1 °C, and Narbonne’s average maximum was 31.7 °C, comparable to 2003 and 2022. Records included Nîmes’ 10 consecutive days >35 °C and a maximum of 41.8 °C, Tarbes’ 39.9 °C, Perpignan’s 29.3 °C night on 29 June, and Narbonne’s 27.8 °C on 16 August, beating the 2003 record of 27.3 °C. Two intense heatwaves occurred: 19 June‑4 July and 8‑18 August. During the first, 35 °C was exceeded 14 times in Nîmes and up to 9 times in Toulouse or Carcassonne; Narbonne had 15 tropical nights (>20 °C), Nîmes 14, Toulouse 10. In the second, temperatures often surpassed 40 °C, with two consecutive days >40 °C in Toulouse and Montauban and two consecutive days in Carcassonne. Nighttime heat was also high, with 7 tropical nights in Carcassonne, 8 in Nîmes, 10 in Toulouse, and up to 11 in Sète or Perpignan.

title: Août 2025, le troisième mois le plus chaud jamais enregistré en Dordogne - ici
content: In August 2025, the Dordogne department experienced its third‑hottest month on record since 1960, following August 2023 and August 2022, according to Météo France data. The average temperature was a little over 22 °C, a degree and a half above normal, as Thierry Godain, a forecaster at Météo France, noted 'ce qui est un degré et demi de plus par rapport à la normale'. A heatwave from 7 to 17 August averaged 35 °C and produced two record peaks. On 11 August every temperature record was broken: 43.5 °C in Monpazier, 42 °C in Périgueux, Bergerac, and the Eyzies, and nearly 42 °C in Montignac‑Lascaux. On 13 August temperatures never fell below 20 °C, with 23.6 °C in Bergerac, which Godain described as '23,6 degrés à Bergerac, ce qui se rapproche d’une nuit tropicale'. The month saw 260 hours of sunshine, 15 % more than normal, '15% de durée d’ensoleillement en plus que la normale'. The region remained very dry until 18 August, when thunderstorms on 19 and 20 August brought some rain. Heavy showers on 29 August raised August’s total rainfall to 63 mm, close to the usual 67 mm, with 30 mm recorded in Saint‑Martin‑de‑Fressengeas and Terrasson‑Lavilledieu and up to 50 mm in some spots.

title: Météo : un record de 1976 battu en Sarthe
content: During summer 2025, the Sarthe department experienced unusually hot, sunny, and dry conditions. Total rainfall over June‑August was 112.3 mm, 27 % below the 153.5 mm normal, according to Météo France. The driest station was Saint‑Germain with 96.2 mm, while Marolles‑les‑Braults recorded 176.2 mm, including a single‑day 71 mm storm on 20 August. Temperatures were above normal: minima 15.5 °C, 1.6 °C higher than the seasonal average, and maxima 27.8 °C, 2.6 °C above normal. The summer ranked fourth hottest since 1945, after 2003 (record 28.5 °C), 2022, and 2018. The hottest day was 1 July (38.2 °C at Le Mans, 38.6 °C at Saint‑Cornille); the coldest maximum was 20 August. The department set a new record of 32 days with temperatures ≥30 °C, surpassing the 30‑day record of 1976. Sunshine hours reached 795, 17 % above the 680‑hour normal, making it the fourth sunniest summer since 1991, after 2022 (867 h). Laurent Belsœur, a forecaster at Météo France, noted that 'l'été n'a pas été assez arrosé'.

title: 法国气象局:今夏为该国有记录以来第三热夏季
content: The French Meteorological Service released a bulletin on 2 September 2025 stating that the summer of 2025 was the third hottest on record, with an average temperature of 22.2 °C, 1.9 °C above the long‑term mean. The season experienced 27 heat‑wave days, ranking second only to 2022’s 33 days. June was exceptionally hot, 3.3 °C above normal; July and August were 0.9 °C and 1.4 °C above normal respectively. The consecutive heat waves increased soil dryness and weakened vegetation. Rainfall was lower than normal, with most of western France recording 5–10 fewer rainy days than usual. The bulletin was issued by the French Meteorological Service on 2 September 2025.

title: 法国气象局：今夏为该国有记录以来第三热夏季
content: The French Meteorological Agency released a bulletin on 2 September 2025 stating that the 2025 summer had an average temperature of '22.2 °C', which is '1.9 °C' above the long‑term mean and makes it the third hottest summer on record after 2003 and 2022. The season experienced '27 heat‑wave days', ranking second only to 2022's '33 days'. June was exceptionally hot with an average temperature '3.3 °C' above normal, while July and August were '0.9 °C' and '1.4 °C' above their respective long‑term averages. The consecutive heat waves intensified soil dryness, rendering vegetation more vulnerable. Additionally, rainfall was below average, with most of western France recording '5–10 fewer rainy days' than the long‑term mean.

title: En Gironde, la fin de la canicule est proche... il reste encore une dernière journée étouffante
content: The second heatwave of the summer is coming to an end in Gironde, with a vigilance orange maintained until Sunday, August 17th at midnight. According to Météo-France, temperatures will reach 35 degrees Celsius in Bordeaux this afternoon, which is about 7 degrees above the seasonal norms. The vigilance orange for the heatwave will remain in effect until tonight, midnight, before cooler temperatures arrive. On Sunday, the morning will be cloudy, followed by a clearer sky, with temperatures reaching 28 degrees Celsius in Arcachon, 31 degrees in the Médoc, and up to 37 degrees in Bordeaux and Langon. A cooling trend is expected to begin on Monday, August 18th, and especially on Tuesday, August 19th. Météo France predicts a very cloudy morning on Monday, with a cloudy sky for most of the day. Some sunshine is expected on Tuesday, before rain arrives mid-week. Showers are forecast for Wednesday, August 20th and Thursday, August 21st, with temperatures returning to seasonal norms, around 28 degrees Celsius in the afternoon in Bordeaux and elsewhere in Gironde.

title: Météo. Après des jours de chaleurs, une baisse des températures annoncée à Toulouse et en Occitanie
content: After a week of scorching heat in Toulouse and Occitanie, Météo-France is predicting a drop in temperatures for Monday, August 18, 2025. According to the weather service, temperatures in Toulouse are expected to reach 33°C, a significant decrease from the almost record-breaking highs of the previous week. The sky is expected to be mostly cloudy, with a risk of thunderstorms in the evening. In other parts of Occitanie, temperatures are also expected to decrease, but the heat will still be felt in coastal cities, with temperatures reaching 38°C in Alès and Nîmes, and 35°C in Perpignan. Météo-France's forecast is as follows: 34°C in Cahors, 30°C in Laguiole, and 28°C in Saint-Gaudens. The sky will be mostly cloudy throughout the day, with a risk of thunderstorms in the evening and overnight.

title: Eté 2025 : au 3ème rang des plus chauds, jusqu'à 43°C dans le sud-ouest - Actualités La Chaîne Météo
content: The 2025 summer in France was the third warmest on record, with an average temperature about +2 °C above the 1991‑2020 baseline. The heat began early, with June 2025 ranking second among June months, and a sustained heatwave from 19 June to 4 July – the 50th such event since 1947. Heat‑wave alerts covered 84 departments, 16 of them red. On 30 June and 1 July the national thermal index hit 28.2 °C, exceeding historical records by more than +7 °C over seasonal normals. The first half of the season (1 June‑15 July) was the hottest ever recorded since 1930. The 40 °C threshold was breached in three summer months, and a new 51st heatwave ran from 8‑18 August. In the south‑west and Mediterranean basin, temperatures surpassed 40 °C in the shade, with record highs in Angoulême (41.2 °C), Bordeaux (41.6 °C), Bergerac (42.1 °C), and Argeliers/Montpazier (43.4 °C). Toulouse saw 35 °C for ten consecutive days, a first since August 2003. The season underscores the trend of climate warming, with 7 of the 10 warmest French summers occurring in the last decade (2015‑2025).

title: Records de chaleur : pourquoi les 50 °C ne sont plus impossibles...
content: While temperatures above 40°C are common in France during the summer, it is possible that the country could reach temperatures of 50°C in the future. According to Météo France, the temperature record in France is 46°C, set in Vérargues in 2019. However, to reach 50°C, an additional 4°C would be needed. While the climate is warming rapidly, Météo France predicts that the 40°C threshold will be reached annually around 2100, and that local records of 50°C 'are possible as early as 2050' and 'probable' by the end of the century. It is therefore possible that certain departments in southern France could reach 50°C within the next 25 years. As Météo France notes, 'it is not the real temperature that is felt, but the perceived temperature, which can already reach or exceed 50°C in the south of France during heatwaves associated with humid air.'
